caption: Rules, and what Ordinance DS does

rows.does: Every text colour is measured against its surface, in both themes.
The edge of a control and the focus outline are measured against the page.
A status is a tag with words, and a link is underlined.
The first link of a page skips to the content.

rows.rule: WCAG 2.2, 2.4.2 Page Titled, and 3.1.1 Language of Page
rows.does: Every page has a title and says its language.
Headings come in order, and every table has a caption and column heads.
The menu and the help are parts of HTML that open with the keyboard.
A button and an item in the menu are at least 24 px high, from one token.
The time tokens are zero when the reader asks for reduced motion.
This European standard refers to WCAG for web pages, so the rows above apply.
A page loads nothing from another server, and a script may not store anything in the browser.
A page runs no code that is written into it, and the server sends a strict security policy.

rows.rule: EU Cyber Resilience Act, Annex I
rows.does: Every file from another project is listed with a checksum, and the build writes a bill of materials.
The list of third-party files and the bill of materials name what the site is made of.
A change must pass the check, and the same sources always give the same site.
The pages are checked against plain-language rules.
